title: Protection
author: Upstairs_Trader
selftext: What is everyone doing if their position ends up unprotected for whatever reason. How are you all getting your bots to detect and repair or close the position asap?

comments.author: Brilliant_Potato4158
comments.body: stop loss on order to api, bunch of other kill switches. you could also ping the endpoint after your order is placed to check if a SL is on else add it but i don’t think i’ve ever had an issue with a SL not being on if in the payload unless there’s a bug in my code…

replies.author: Upstairs_Trader
replies.body: I’m not a coder, but have been using codex and Claude to help along the way and it seems this is my only issue. There are times when the order is submitted, accepted then I get a notification it has no stop or target. So somewhere along the way the broker dropped the stop loss and I have no idea why. I would rather find a fix to avoid the stop loss being dropped, but if not, I would love to at least have it protected.

replies.author: Brilliant_Potato4158
replies.body:
well no SL is naked and you are putting the system at risk…

well maybe there’s a missing parameter? i would either do a plan with claude and throw in the brokers api docs as a reference or download it to disk and point claude at it. i would also test it thoroughly in a demo account…. if there’s a logic bug good luck as that could take a while to pinpoint…. or just throw a stronger model at it but even then i wouldn’t fully trust any AI stuff with real money… you would wanna understand your codebase if you’re putting down real money since all it takes is one bad trade that turns catastrophic.

replies.author: Upstairs_Trader
replies.body: Yeah, I’m trying to figure it out, because when it runs well, I have profitable days until two or three orders. Just have no stop loss and everything is down the hill from there. So what I’ve been doing is actually sitting there and watching it and monitoring it while working with the AI and closing positions immediately.

replies.author: Brilliant_Potato4158
replies.body: get the error code and message from under broker’s api response then smash it into claude, presto.

replies.author: Upstairs_Trader
replies.body: I’m going to check that out and see what it tells me.

comments.author: Upstairs_Trader
comments.body: I think the issue is sometimes the broker accepts the entry but then reject the other orders and I don’t know why

comments.author: Upstairs_Trader
comments.body: I hadn’t read the documentation of the API online, but I will try to download it and see

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: a reconcile loop, not a repair step inside the strategy. every few minutes the bot pulls the real position list from the broker, compares it with what it believes it holds, and anything on the broker side with no matching stop gets one of two treatments: a stop at the rule's level if the rule still applies, flattened if it doesn't. the strategy never gets a vote, because the strategy is what lost track in the first place. I built Quantradin with this exact failure in mind: the bot's key can close or cancel but never open, so the repair path can only shrink the book. quantradin.com, paper throughout.

replies.author: Upstairs_Trader
replies.body: I like this idea, I’m going to run it in the AI and see what it says. Is it all right if I message you in case I have issues

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: sure, message me, or ask here so the next person with the same problem finds the answer. when you run it, start with the compare step alone and log what it finds for a day before you let it place a single stop.
